reason: The goal calls for a fluid to carry supplies, so I’ll start with water, salts and plasma proteins.

reason: I'll add stored nutrients to the plasma to build its transport function.
expectation: I expect nutrient-containing plasma, though I'm unsure whether it will count as blood yet.

effect: The completed blood combines transport, defense and clotting roles; the result also clarifies that blood does not normally clot in an undamaged vessel.
reaction: The final explanation brought the components together, though I would have liked more detail about how white cells and clotting work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making red blood cells was most worthwhile: the picture describes their development and loss of nuclei, and the text connects haemoglobin to oxygen delivery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grouping platelets with clotting proteins felt like an extra assembly step because the result did not explain how they work together.

surprise.text: I was interested that developing red blood cells lose their nuclei as they mature.

arbitrary.text: Combining platelets and clotting proteins before adding them to blood felt somewhat arbitrary; their grouping was clear, but its purpose was not explained at that point.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in another chapter to see how blood connects the arm to other body systems, although several combinations here were predictable and briefly explained.
